findings.title: Item resume imports private functions from the CLI module through a cycle
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` imports `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` from `run.py` inside the function, and needs two `reportPrivateUsage` suppressions to do it. `run.py` also imports `run_item`, so the two modules depend on each other. The code comment admits this. Move those helpers to a shared module, or pass them in as arguments (the `run_body` argument already works this way). That removes the cycle and the suppressions.

findings.title: `_execute_each_step` and `execute_pipeline` keep growing
findings.description: `_execute_each_step` is well over 50 lines after this change. It now handles source evaluation, item reruns, pre-flagging, flag-kind classification, halt capture, per-item report writes and final report writes. `_finish_each_report` takes six parameters. The `item_rerun` flag is also threaded through `execute_pipeline`, `_execute_step` and `_execute_each_step`, so rerun mode is an extra branch in the main path rather than a separate strategy. Extract the per-item body, and consider a small "item source and report sink" abstraction. That would let the normal run and the rerun differ in one place instead of in several conditionals.

findings.title: Mutating-step detection relies on a hard-coded step list and loose dict shapes
findings.description: `pipeline_mutates` uses a fixed set (`DESIGN`, `TASKS`, `IMPLEMENT`, `DEVLOG`, `BRANCH`) plus the string key `commit_each_iteration`. A new mutating step type that is not added here silently runs without the lock, and nothing fails to flag it. The nested-step walk casts `config["steps"]` items as `{type: config}` dicts and treats any unexpected shape as non-mutating. That is a silent fallback, and the project rules say not to use those. Prefer a mutating property declared on each step type, or make an unknown shape raise. The `commit_each_iteration` literal should also be a shared constant, since the loop config defines it too.

findings.title: `_write_each_report` breaks the 104-column line limit
findings.description: `async def _write_each_report(report: BatchReport, runs_dir: Path | None, *, final: bool = True) -> None:` is over the configured `line-length = 104` (pyproject.toml:71), so `ruff check` (E501) or `ruff format --check` will fail. Other new lines are also long, for example in `test_run_lock_cli.py` and `test_item_resume_source.py`. Run `ruff format` on the changed files.

findings.title: Each-step report is rewritten after every item with a blocking pattern per item
findings.description: Writing the report after each item is intended, since a killed batch should leave a report. Each write does two atomic writes (Markdown and JSON, each with a temp file and rename) and runs in `asyncio.to_thread`, so the event loop is not blocked. There is no `fsync`, though. The "never see a partial file" claim holds, but after a crash a renamed file can be empty on some filesystems. The `final=False` path also swallows nothing: an `OSError` from the per-item write propagates out of the loop. That choice is reasonable, but the documentation says "failure leaves the previous report intact", so the batch ending because of a report write failure should be stated in the docs and covered by a test. I could not find such a test in the diff.

findings.title: `BatchReport.load` and `from_json` accept loosely typed JSON
findings.description: `report.json` is an external file boundary, and the project rules call for Pydantic there. The code uses manual `cast` calls and `str(values[...])`. A missing `"index"` becomes the string `"None"` instead of an error, because `str(None)` does not raise and `data.get` is used. Missing `outcome` is caught (`ItemOutcome("None")` raises `ValueError`), but `index` and `name` are not. Use a Pydantic model, or fail explicitly when required keys are absent.

findings.title: Resume paths in `run.py` all share the pipeline definition lock check
findings.description: Every `_locked(definition, ...)` call uses a `definition` that is assigned in that same branch (lines 1153, 1179, 1217, 1271). The lock is therefore taken against the right pipeline. This is fine as it stands. Because `_locked` closes the coroutine on a failed lock, nothing is left unawaited.

findings.title: Test coverage is strong for the new paths
findings.description: The diff adds tests for the lock (held, killed holder, worktrees, open failure), report round-trip and version mismatch, flag-kind classification, halt reporting, the dependency ordering and cycles, reserved params, and the item-resume flows against a real temp git repo. Each failure-mode test asserts an observable signal such as an ERROR log or an exit code. This meets the failure-mode enumeration rule.

structured_findings.summary: Item resume imports private functions from the CLI module through a cycle
Mutating-step detection relies on a hard-coded step list and loose dict shapes
Each-step report is rewritten after every item with a blocking pattern per item
Resume paths in `run.py` all share the pipeline definition lock check
Test coverage is strong for the new paths
